defects.summary: Expiry releases reserved units via db.adjustReserved without invalidating the availability TTL cache that checkAvailability reads.
defects.trigger: Create a reservation (which warms the availability cache), wait until it expires, run expireStaleReservations, then immediately call checkAvailability for the same SKU.
defects.impact: Storefront keeps reporting the held (lower) availability after the hold has already been released, so customers cannot buy stock that is free.
defects.howDetectable: expireStaleReservations adjusts reserved directly and never calls availabilityCache.invalidate; compare with holdStock/releaseStock/consumeStock in inventory.js which all invalidate after mutating reserved/onHand.

defects.summary: Check-then-act race: availability is read from a snapshot, then an await happens before writing reserved, so two concurrent holds can both succeed against the same unit.
defects.trigger: Seed a SKU with onHand=1, reserved=0. Fire two holdStock(sku, 1) calls (or two createReservation for different orders) without awaiting the first.
defects.impact: Reserved can exceed onHand; the same physical unit is sold twice (oversell).
defects.howDetectable: readStock returns a copy; appendAudit is awaited between the availability check and putStock of the mutated copy. Concurrent callers both observe available>=qty and both write reserved+=qty. Main-branch holdStock used synchronous getStock+adjustReserved without a yield in between.

defects.summary: Requested refund amounts are returned as-is without capping to the remaining unpaid balance, violating requirements rule 11.
defects.trigger: Order paidAmount=100 with refundedTotal=80; call resolveRefundAmount(order, 80) or refundOrder(id, 80).
defects.impact: A second partial refund can push refundedTotal above paidAmount, over-refunding the customer.
defects.howDetectable: remaining is computed but never used as an upper bound; the function returns roundMoney(requested) whenever requested>0. docs/requirements.md rule 11 requires the sum of refunds never exceed the paid amount.

defects.summary: Volume tiers use exclusive > comparisons, so orders of exactly 10 or exactly 50 units get no / wrong discount versus the inclusive thresholds in the spec.
defects.trigger: Call volumeDiscountRate(10) and volumeDiscountRate(50), or computeOrderTotal with 10 and 50 units.
defects.impact: Customers at the published tier boundaries do not receive the advertised 5%/10% discounts.
defects.howDetectable: Code uses units > 50 and units > 10; docs/requirements.md rule 8 and TC-06 require inclusive bounds (>=10 for 5%, >=50 for 10%).

defects.summary: Payment gateway failures are caught, logged, and replaced with a synthetic local receipt; the ledger is still updated and the caller receives ok:true.
defects.impact: Caller and ledger treat a failed gateway refund as successful; money is marked refunded without the payment provider paying out (and rule 12 is violated).
defects.howDetectable: catch block builds a localOnly receipt and falls through to refundedTotal/status mutation and return { ok: true }. docs/requirements.md rule 12 requires failure to leave the ledger untouched and return a failure result.

defects.summary: Lock release is not in a finally block; if the critical section throws, releaseLock is skipped and the key stays held forever.
defects.trigger: createReservation with a malformed line (missing unitPrice) so computeOrderTotal throws inside withLock for order:ORD-4; then retry the same order id with a valid line.
defects.impact: Subsequent operations on the same lock key hang indefinitely (wedged order/reservation).
defects.howDetectable: Main-branch withLock wrapped fn in try/finally; feature branch awaits fn then calls releaseLock only on the success path. docs/requirements.md rule 14 and TC-10 require release on error.

defects.summary: Commit no longer sets reservation.status to COMMITTED, so expireStaleReservations still treats the reservation as HELD and can release/consume stock a second time.
defects.trigger: Commit a reservation whose expiresAt is already in the past (or set a short ttlMs), then run expireStaleReservations.
defects.impact: Reserved counter is decremented again after commit already released the hold, understating reserved / overstating availability and corrupting stock accounting.
defects.howDetectable: commitReservation writes committedAt but leaves status as HELD (main set status='COMMITTED'). expireStaleReservations only skips when status !== 'HELD', so the combination across the two functions breaks the single-release invariant.

traps.whyItLooksWrong: Adding Number.EPSILON before Math.round looks like a magic hack that could round the wrong way.
traps.whyItIsActuallyCorrect: Binary floats store values like 1.005 as slightly under 1.005; the epsilon nudge restores half-up behaviour required by rule 10, and the comment documents the finance reconciliation reason.

traps.whyItLooksWrong: No null/undefined guard on getStock(sku) before reading row.reserved — looks like a crash waiting to happen.
traps.whyItIsActuallyCorrect: All callers (cancel/commit/create rollback) only release SKUs from holds that were successfully placed, so the row is guaranteed to exist; the JSDoc states that contract.

traps.whyItLooksWrong: Only Math.min against the max — looks like it fails to clamp a zero/negative or missing lower bound.
traps.whyItIsActuallyCorrect: Rule 1 only requires clamping to a maximum of 60 minutes; defaulting undefined to 15 minutes and capping the upper bound fully satisfies the written spec.

traps.whyItLooksWrong: Deleting and re-inserting the key, then dropping keys().next(), looks like it might evict the entry just written or use an arbitrary order.
traps.whyItIsActuallyCorrect: Map iteration is insertion-ordered; delete+reinsert moves an updated key to the newest position, so keys().next() is the least-recently-written entry and the size check runs after the insert, so the new entry is never the eviction victim when size is exactly MAX_ENTRIES+1.
